title: Deterministic request-replay tracing adapter for postmortem debugging
creator: Dana Kim
description:
Background:

On-call and SRE teams frequently need to reproduce production request flows to investigate regressions and flakey behaviors that surface only under real request interleavings. Current tracing captures rich spans and context, but it lacks a lightweight, deterministic way to replay a single request's spans (including sampling decisions, injected headers, and important derived attributes) so that local or staging services can reproduce the same causal path for debugging.

Objective:

Build an SDK + middleware tracing adapter that records a compact, deterministic replay token alongside the normal span data. The replay token must be sufficient to reconstruct request headers, sampling metadata, order of downstream calls, and key KV-cache hits/misses to enable deterministic replay in a debug harness. The adapter should be opt-in per-environment and preserve privacy by allowing field-level filters and redaction rules.

Non-goals:

- Not intended to replace full request capture systems (e.g., full recorded HTTP bodies).
- Not adding heavy-weight deterministic simulation of GPUs/runtime scheduling.

Acceptance criteria:

1) SDK instrumentation emits a "replay_token" header when enabled and preserves this token in traces and logs.
2) A separate replay artifact (small JSON line) can be exported to S3/Drive that contains the token, list of downstream endpoints called (in order), sampling decisions, and filtered attribute snapshots. Size target: < 20KB per trace.
3) Local replay harness (in repo as a test binary) can ingest the artifact and exert the same sequence of SDK hooks so that end-to-end request flow is reproduced deterministically against a test instance.
4) Redaction filters configurable via Console feature flag; by default PII keys are removed.

Design notes and trade-offs:

- Token format: base64-encoded protobuf v2 with stable field ordering to guarantee deterministic decoding. Use a compact delta-encoding for downstream call timestamps (relative offsets) to keep size small.
- We will avoid including payload bodies by default; instead include body fingerprints (SHA256 prefix) and allow opt-in capture via admin Console for debug sessions.
- Determinism boundary: the harness will mock time, RNG seeds, and external client backoffs so that the same sequence of SDK events is replayed. This requires SDK to expose deterministic hooks and pluggable adapters.
- Storage: artifacts are uploaded to the existing observability artifact bucket under a "replay/" prefix with per-team ACLs.

Implementation plan:

1) SDK changes (Go/Node/Python): add a lightweight replay collector interface that records ordered events (child spans start/finish, outgoing HTTP call metadata, sampling decision) and emits the replay_token header when tracing is enabled for replay.
2) Middleware adapters: Express/Koa middleware and net/http wrapper for Go that append necessary events to collector.
3) Exporter: add a small exporter in the tracing pipeline that writes compact replay artifacts to the artifact store and associates artifact id with trace id in trace span tags.
4) Local harness: repo/tooling/trace-replay harness that consumes artifact and replays calls using deterministic client fakes and SDK test doubles.
5) Console integration: feature flag to enable replay capture, redaction config UI, and a list view for replay artifacts on a trace page.

Testing & validation:

- Unit tests for collector determinism and token roundtrip encoding/decoding across languages.
- Integration test: run replay harness against a staging service with seeded RNG/time and verify identical span tree and attribute sets.
- Load impact: ensure additional per-request overhead < 1% p95 latency in standard e2e benchmark when replay disabled; when enabled, overhead target < 5% p95.

Rollout plan:

- Stage 1 (canary): enable replay artifacts for internal dev team only. Monitor artifact store growth and latency impact.
- Stage 2 (beta): enable opt-in for early enterprise customers; gather feedback on redaction defaults.
- Stage 3 (general availability): enable via Console for teams with proper ACLs and storage quotas.

Monitoring & metrics:

Emit metrics for: replay-enabled request ratio, artifact size histogram, replay-export success/failure rate, and additional p95 latency delta when enabled. Dashboard: add "Trace Replay" panel under Observability -> Tracing showing artifact counts, sizes, and failures.

Security & privacy:

- Redaction pipeline runs before artifacts are stored; default deny-list for PII keys.
- Artifacts encrypted at rest using customer key where applicable.
- Security review required before GA and export to external artifact stores.

Acceptance test links and artifacts:

- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Replay+Design+Notes
- Design mockups (Console): https://drive.google.com/example/replay-console-mock
- Local harness prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/4821
- Artifact dashboard prototype: https://console.redwood.ai/d/trace-replay/prototype

Next steps:

- Finalize replay token protobuf schema with schema-review team (due 2026-02-23).
- Spin up SDK PRs (Go first) and share design with SDK owners.
- Create a minimal internal-only canary to validate performance and storage costs.
